checks.check: No native nested tuple key construction

manual_findings.argument: Each hashable key node receives a scalar equality-class integer. A tuple key record encodes arity and ordered child equality-class integers, never the native child tuples. Dictionary collision membership hashes only those scalar class IDs. Repeated tuple descendants reuse one class, removing the stated recursive native tuplehash path.
manual_findings.id: No tuple unfolding in collision hash

manual_findings.argument: None uses a disjoint marker. False/True and integers normalize to exact ratios0/1 or1/1 or n/1; finite floats use the builtin exact reduced ratio. Thus bool/int/equal finite float keys collide as native keys should; signed zero normalizes together, while strict original value nodes retain their own type/hex. The manually reviewed claim assumes documented exact finite scalar conversion, not a runtime float probe.

Strings use exact surrogatepass bytes and explicit length, disjoint from ratio/None/tuple markers. Tuple records contain minimal unsigned arity and child class encodings. Induction over earlier child references makes exact class equality equivalent to native finite hashable-key equality; ordered multiplicity is preserved.

String-only dictionary fields preserve original ordered names. Other dictionaries use entries returning complete typed key/value cursors; no unsupported native tuple materialization is hidden in fields. Full native matches remains strict type/container/order correspondence.

The particular exponential tuplehash recurrence is removed. This is not a useful whole resource bound: recursion depth, bytes/integers/hash-table operations, canonicalization/parser/checker/native-original traversals and all worker/outer custody costs still require full analysis. No400m/128MiB/180s/RSS fit or complete generic resource theorem follows.

prospective_unrun_controls: Shared binary tuple DAG keys across allowed depths; no native tuple hash is invoked.
False/0/0.0 and True/1/1.0 collision controls, signed zero and finite nonintegral/large ratio boundaries.
Nested tuple numeric-equivalent keys, order/multiplicity differences and tuple/string/None disjointness.
Mixed general-key dictionaries via entries plus strict complete native matching; malformed/unhashable key refusal.
Quota/fault cutoffs retain actual parser/work/wire/error and complete available prefix.
